expression-document.comment: A raw expression root cannot acquire item ownership when recovery reaches a declaration-shaped line; its remaining tail keeps lexical roles.

ambiguous-recursive-call.comment: Only an identifier after the marker or its complete annotation group proves recursion. A later line can instead complete an ordinary reference or call.

ambiguous-root-rec.comment: A raw rec prefix can become an expression or a recursive declaration on a later line. Return to file-root dispatch only after its group/callee boundary is known.

ambiguous-minus-before-number.comment: Whether a flush `-` belongs to the following number depends on the preceding significant token, including across comments and newlines. TextMate cannot reconstruct that lexer state, so it deliberately leaves only the minus byte unscoped; the digits still receive the numeric scope below.
ambiguous-minus-before-number.name: meta.ambiguous-leading-minus.kio

elaborator-bang-call.comment: A contiguous value-reference-plus-bang token is an elaborator call for highlighting. The head follows the canonical word shape, including reserved references; a reserved prefix alone supplies no special role. A space before `!` keeps the identifier and operator tokens separate.
elaborator-bang-call.name: entity.name.function.macro.elaborator.kio

module-decl.comment: Match a `module <path>;` declaration so path segments — including keyword-spelled ones like `op` or `let` — paint as entity.name.module instead of inheriting the keyword.declaration scope from the catch-all rule.

import-decl.comment: Positive head scopes require a same-line provider path and selection/as/builtin tail. Slash-led segments shield contextual names; nested selections and groups protect their delimiters.

label-forward-decl.comment: Refine a complete same-line braced type-forward declaration. Interstitial comments or incomplete and multiline heads retain ordinary neutral token coverage.

row-let.comment: Keep contextual `as` recognition across multiline row-let entries; the entry state consumes the label before the alias state can classify the separator, including duplicate spellings and intervening comments.

row-let-entry.comment: Start only at an entry boundary and consume the label path, so a label spelled `as` cannot be mistaken for the separator.

row-let-label-segment.comment: Consume each dotted label segment across trivia before alias recognition resumes; the segment stays neutral in this regex-only layer.

row-let-alias.comment: The first `as` after a consumed label path is the separator; remain in this state across trivia until the binder arrives.

ambiguous-import-head.comment: Unproven line-split or incomplete import heads remain neutral. Recovery stops at the terminator or a following independently recognizable declaration.
ambiguous-import-head.name: meta.ambiguous-declaration.kio

ambiguous-op-head.comment: Without complete same-line pattern evidence, do not guess keyword roles for the head or a later callable body. Empty ordinary op calls stay outside this state.
ambiguous-op-head.name: meta.ambiguous-declaration.kio

call-head.comment: Shield keyword-shaped call names such as `add(...)` from the catch-all keyword rule; TextMate normalization treats function names as identifiers for agreement.
call-head.name: entity.name.function.kio

slot.comment: `_`, `__`, `___` slot tokens in `op` patterns. Four or more underscores are reserved and not matched here.
slot.name: variable.parameter.slot.kio

operator-arrow.comment: Function-type arrow and fixed-role dot-splice operators. These are exact spellings, not prefixes of larger symbol-runs. A dot-splice may immediately follow an identifier-plus-bang elaborator token, as in the bare `transform!.<value` form consumed by the earlier elaborator rule.
operator-arrow.name: keyword.operator.arrow.kio

operator-row-suffix.comment: Row access/update suffix tokens. Classified as user operators to match the reference token dump.
operator-row-suffix.name: keyword.operator.user.kio

operator-builtin.comment: Standalone built-in operators. Multi-char runs containing these chars are user-declared operators and fall through to `operator-user`.
operator-builtin.name: keyword.operator.kio

operator-user.comment: A symbol run stops before a comment or second slash; a standalone dot is a separator.
operator-user.name: keyword.operator.user.kio

label-value-shorthand.comment: TextMate refines the unambiguous adjacent shorthand (`{item}`); it leaves whitespace-bearing braces unrefined because a stateless grammar cannot distinguish label shorthand from an ordinary block.

varop-mirror-bracket.comment: Each adjacent OPEN character pushes its mirrored CLOSE onto the rule stack. Only the innermost frame admits split whitespace; outer frames require adjacent closing characters.

recursive-annotation-item-tokens.comment: Only an item's first identifier is an annotation slot; its lexical tail ends at the outer comma or close, and nested groups cannot create slots.

proved-ordinary-recursive-arguments.comment: A locally closed ordinary call retains expression roles inside nested argument groups.
